title: Outlook: Cloud Policy controls for Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the planned Outlook controls from existing Cloud Policy and mailbox policies. The Exchange admin center route and signature command are documented; the general Cloud Policy wizard path needs a minor completion for group selection.

claims.quote: We’re introducing Cloud Policy service support for Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows.

claims.claim: Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Choose the scope > specific groups > Configure Settings reaches the general Cloud Policy settings wizard in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. On the Policy configurations page, select Create. To add groups, select Add Groups and choose the relevant groups. On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration.

claims.quote: Searched: Cloud Policy configurations Microsoft Graph PowerShell API create update Outlook; officeCloudPolicy policyConfigurations Graph API. Read Cloud Policy overview and Outlook policy management; Graph results describe other policy families, not this control.

claims.claim: The All Accounts Configuration setting is reached in Microsoft 365 Apps admin center through Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Configure Settings > Show All Accounts view for users with multiple accounts in Outlook for Windows > Configuration setting.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. Create a policy configuration, or edit an existing one, and target the group of users you want to manage. On Configure Settings, search for Show All Accounts view for users with multiple accounts in Outlook for Windows.

claims.claim: Exchange admin center > Roles > Outlook web app policies > policy > Features > Manage Features > User experience > Email signature reaches the signature availability control.
claims.quote: click on the name of the policy > select Manage Features in the Features section > expand the User experience section > uncheck Email signature

claims.claim: Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -SignaturesEnabled $false prevents Outlook on the web users from manually creating email signatures.
claims.quote: Admins can use either of the following methods to prevent Outlook on the web users from manually creating email signatures: Exchange PowerShell: Use the SignaturesEnabled parameter with the value $false on the Set-OwaMailboxPolicy cmdlet.

claims.claim: An existing Cloud Policy setting manages the default All Accounts view in new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: Use Cloud Policy to choose whether All Accounts is shown by default in new Outlook for Windows and whether users can change that behavior.

claims.claim: Configuration setting must be Enabled first to activate the All Accounts policy.
claims.quote: Open the policy and set Configuration setting to Enabled. This activates the policy; the additional settings below determine the view and whether users can change it.

claims.claim: Configure the unified inbox view chooses whether All Accounts is shown or hidden.
claims.quote: The first column is Configure the unified inbox view; the second is Allow user to override this setting. Enabled | Enabled | Show All Accounts by default. Users can change it. Disabled | Enabled | Hide All Accounts by default. Users can change it.

claims.claim: Allow user to override this setting determines whether users can change the configured All Accounts behaviour.
claims.quote: When user override is disabled, the policy controls the view and users can't change the configured behavior.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy can enforce Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise settings on devices that are not domain joined or otherwise managed.
claims.quote: Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365 lets you enforce policy settings for Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise on a user's device, even if the device isn't domain joined or otherwise managed.

claims.claim: Some Cloud Policy settings can be enforced for Office for the web.
claims.quote: You can also enforce some policy settings for Office for the web and Loop, both for guests who are signed in and for users who access documents anonymously.

claims.claim: Learn says most existing Outlook Cloud policies apply only to classic Outlook.
claims.quote: All ADMX policies and most policies from Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365 (Cloud policies) apply only to classic Outlook.

claims.claim: Most Outlook on the web and new Outlook settings are currently managed through Exchange mailbox policies rather than the planned defaults expansion.
claims.quote: You can manage most features with Exchange PowerShell cmdlets. Most of the mailbox policies apply to both Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows, so you can't enable them on one client but not the other.

claims.where: Risk assessment / Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Cloud Policy applies only to user objects, not device objects.
claims.quote: Policies only apply to user objects. A group might contain both device objects and user objects, but the device objects are ignored.

claims.where: Risk assessment / Security & identity; Governance guidance / Before rollout
claims.claim: Targeted user objects must be present in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: User objects must be present in Microsoft Entra ID and have a supported license assigned.

claims.where: Risk assessment / Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: User objects must have a supported licence assigned for Cloud Policy to apply.
claims.quote: User objects must be present in Microsoft Entra ID and have a supported license assigned.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy configurations can target Microsoft Entra groups and apply according to user membership.
claims.quote: When the service receives the check-in call, Microsoft Entra group membership is determined for the user. If the user is a member of a Microsoft Entra group that is assigned a policy configuration, the service returns the appropriate policy settings for the user

claims.claim: Cloud Policy supports nested groups up to three levels deep.
claims.quote: Nested groups support up to three levels deep.

claims.claim: The first account added to new Outlook is considered the primary account.
claims.quote: Several App-wide settings, including Theme, Text Size and Spacing, and Diagnostic Data and Connected Experiences are associated with the first account added in new Outlook. This account is considered as the primary account.

claims.claim: App-wide settings such as Theme, Diagnostic Data and Connected Experiences depend on the primary account.
claims.quote: While policies can be applied to any organization account in new Outlook, management of app-wide settings requires the designated account to be set as primary. For example, Theme, Diagnostic Data, and Connected Experiences.

claims.where: Risk assessment / Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance / At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Cloud Policy priority determines which conflicting policy setting applies when a user is in multiple targeted groups.
claims.quote: If the user is a member of multiple Microsoft Entra groups with conflicting policy settings, priority is used to determine which policy setting is applied. The highest priority is applied, with "0" being the highest priority that you can assign.
